sections.text: Ancestor Spirit is found in an isolated arena accessible from Siofra River. To access it, you must light all eight obelisks by the stairs to the Hallowhorn Grounds east of the Siofra River Bank Site of Grace. When you've done so, the deer carcass at the back of the temple will glow and you can interact with it to teleport just outside the boss's arena. Walk through the fog gate to fight the boss. The pillars are: By the Siofra River Bank site of grace. Map Link In a corner to the west of the first pillar. Map Link On a small island in the watery area with the lightning wisps.

sections.text: Cleanrot Knight Fight Strategy The Best Tips for Cleanrot Knight: Don't just keep attacking over and over—once it uses Spear Guard, back off or it'll counter-attack. Use Fire Pots . It's very weak to fire and has low health to begin with, so a single pot will do a lot of damage even at low levels Long windups and attack animations leave it very vulnerable to backstabs Melee Users Baiting: Stay close and towards its left to tempt it into using Spear Stab, Impale, or Sacred Phalanx. When it starts winding up one of these slow attacks, circle around behind it and get a backstab critical.

sections.heading: Elden Ring Commander Niall Boss Guide
sections.text: Commander Niall Fight Strategy The Best Tips for Commander Niall Niall will primarily focus on buffing his allies while they are still alive and will perform relatively simple attacks that are easily avoided. Focus on the dual greatsword Knight with at the beginning, as it is more aggressive than the shield Knight. Charming one of the Knights with Bewitching Branches can make the first phase quite simple. sections.heading: Elden Ring Crucible Knight Ordovis Boss Guide
sections.text: Crucible Knight Ordovis Fight Strategy Melee Users Spearfishing: Focus on killing the Crucible Knight with the spear first, since it has the best reach and is best at covering distance and disrupting your attacks on the other one. Try to draw it away from Ordovis, and keep pillars between you and Ordovis when you're attacking the spear knight. Don't get greedy: if you get in more than a hit or two at a time, Ordovis will catch up to you and make you regret it.

sections.heading: Crucible Knight Ordovis Notes & Other Trivia
sections.text: Like his counterpart Siluria, Ordovis appears to have been named after an ancient Celtic tribe: the Ordovices, who lived in present-day Wales, and shared a border with the Silures. The ruins of an ancient Thracian fortress named Urdovisa (also Urdoviza) lie near the present-day town of Kiten in Bulgaria. May also be named after the Ordovician Period, a prehistoric epoch of life on Earth, much like the Crucible.

sections.text: Demi-Human Chief Fight Strategy The Best Tips for Demi-Human Chief: Try to fight one Demi-Human Chief at a time. The second one is around a corner, so if you stay near the entrance to the boss room you can usually avoid attracting its attention. Clear out the other Demi-Humans first with ranged attacks or spells. Demi-Human Chiefs have low poise, so your attacks will usually interrupt theirs. sections.heading: Elden Ring Dragonkin Soldier Boss Guide
sections.text: Dragonkin Soldier Boss Video Guide https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sxEAktrJFV4 Dragonkin Soldier Fight Strategy The Best Tips for Dragonkin Soldier: At the start of the fight, the boss is slow to get up, which can allow one to get multiple hard hits in. This can take away a third to half of its HP right off the bat Use Spirit Jellyfish Ashes to distract the boss, since it has a lot of health. If you have obtained Latenna's Spirit Ash , you can place her out of range which allows her to steadily damage the boss from afar.

sections.heading: Dragonkin Soldier Location
sections.text: Head south from the Worshippers' Woods Site of Grace to a collapsed pillar with an Ancestral Follower archer perched on it. Follower the pillar up to its base, where you'll see the Siofra River East waygate. Map Link This waygate will transport you to the plateau in the center of Siofra River. When you arrive, head northwest to the open plain of shallow water, where you'll find the Dragonkin Soldier collapsed in a heap. As you approach, it will rise up and the fight will begin. Map Link You can also reach this boss from the Ancestral Woods Site of Grace by carefully dropping down from above.

sections.text: Elemer of the Briar is at the very top of The Shaded Castle in Altus Plateau . sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Fallingstar Beasts are creatures formed of shiny black rock. They have spiky tails, patches of white fur, and insect-like mandibles. They are found in craters, likely indicating that they plummeted onto the Lands Between from a great distance. The more mature Full-Grown Fallingstar Beast have greater magical abilities, able to control gravity in their vicinity and unleash great magical beams akin to Comet Azur. They can use Gravity-based abilities, much like other enemies associated with meteors and fallen stars such as Alabaster Lords, Onyx Lords, and Withered Astel.

sections.text: Gideon Ofnir is the Tarnished leader of Roundtable Hold and the adoptive father of Nepheli Loux. Called to the Lands Between by the guidance of Grace, Gideon wishes to become Elden Lord. To this end he accumulates information on the Shardbearers, employing a network of spies to aid in his hunt for knowledge. Initially, he is apprehensive of the Tarnished, but after they have claimed a Great Rune he becomes willing to share his knowledge of the remaining shardbearers.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - The Omenkiller in the Village of the Albinaurics is implied by Nepheli to be one of Gideon's agents. Due to the connection between Omenkillers and perfumers, the Depraved Perfumer in the village may be working with the Omenkiller. - Recusant Henricus, an invader in Limgrave, wears the Eye Surcoat which is said to be worn by Gideon's "eyes and ears". The Eye Surcoat can be looted from a corpse in Rykard's boss arena, indicating another agent of Gideon.

sections.heading: Elden Ring Sir Gideon Ofnir, The All-Knowing Boss Guide
sections.text: Sir Gideon Ofnir, The All-Knowing Fight Strategy The Best Tips for Sir Gideon Ofnir, The All-Knowing: Use the Eternal Darkness spell to redirect nearly all his spells Use the Inescapable Frenzy spell to deal major damage during his monologue. Alternatively, Frenzied Burst can prove useful due to long range. Recommended weapon: Erdtree Greatshield Use Spirit Ashes that can quickly close the distance and harass Gideon such as Black Knife Tiche . Use heavy jump attacks to disrupt Gideon's more powerful spells as he channels them.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Magma Wyrm** is a reoccurring boss and non-respawning enemy in Elden Ring and Elden Ring Nightreign. Magma Wyrms are quadrupedal draconic beings with torn, vestigial wings and broad heads. They were once human heroes who partook in Dragon Communion, for which they were cursed to crawl the earth as flightless imitations of Dragons, losing their humanity in the process. They wield scaly greatswords that resemble the jawbones of dragons, and can spew magma from their mouths.

sections.heading: Locations
sections.text: There are two non-boss Magma Wyrms that can be encountered. One is found in the lower part of Volcano Manor, accessible via an elevator near the Temple of Eiglay Site of Grace. The second is found in the Dragon's Pit minor dungeon in Gravesite Plain, found by progressing normally through the dungeon, and going up the stairs through a cave opening.

sections.heading: Elden Ring Mimic Tear Location
sections.text: The Mimic Tear boss is encountered in multiple locations: Mimic Tear can be found behind a mist door to a temple ruin in Nokron, Eternal City . It doesn't attack immediately, but transforms when you approach the it in the middle of the ruin. See it on the Elden Ring Map Here . One is encountered as the Stray Mimic Tear in the secret catacombs under the Hidden Path to the Haligtree . See the location's page for details on how to reach the boss. Despite the slightly different name, this boss functions much the same way as the Mimic Tear . See it on the Elden Ring Map Here .

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Silver Tears are formless, arcane creatures of mimicry that can reshape and harden their liquid metal bodies at will, becoming weapons and even other living organisms. The Nox of the Eternal Cities sought to forge a Lord, and thus the Mimic Tear was born. It immediately assumes the form of the player as they enter the room, complete with their equipped weapons, armor, and spells. Its Stats and Attributes, such as HP, shall also reflect the player's.

sections.heading: Night's Cavalry Combat information
sections.text: Stance : 80 Stance damage reduction: 80% Stance cannot be broken while on horseback Is vulnerable to a critical hit after being stance broken or knocked out of horse The horse and rider have separate health bars, and only the rider needs to be killed to end the fight. Killing the horse causes the rider to fall to the ground and become vulnerable to a dismount critical . After some time, the rider will resummon the horse with its Remount attack. It's much more likely to remount quickly if you move far away from it, so stay close to maximize the amount of time it's in a weakened state.

sections.heading: Elden Ring Night's Cavalry Boss Guide
sections.text: Night's Cavalry Boss Video Guide Night's Cavalry Fight Strategy The Best Tips for Night's Cavalry: Use Lightning Spear to whittle down its health from afar Use Glintstone Arc to hit both the horse and its rider at once Use a weapon with long reach that deals Pierce Damage , such as a Spear or Halberd Knights met at Dragonbarrow and Forbidden Lands can be - with precise maneuvering - tricked into falling from the cliff. Melee Users Fighting on foot is recommended. They're fast enough to match your pace on Torrent, and the extra maneuverability and ability to dodge on foot will help a lot.

sections.heading: Elden Ring Onyx Lord Boss Guide
sections.text: Onyx Lord Fight Strategy The Best Tips for Onyx Lord: Fight him on the outer edges of the arena. Take advantage of his Meteorite's long cast animation. Melee Users Onyx Lord only has a few moves in his repertoire and it is relatively easy to discern his patterns. Consider fighting him on the outer edges of the arena as the center has uneven terrain which can cause his meteorites to impact with the ground near you, dealing splash damage. Onyx Lord has three main attack patterns: Meteorite, Slice and Dice, and Gravity Well. He will rarely diverge from these attacks.

sections.heading: Starscourge Radahn Notes & Trivia
sections.text: Upon release, Radahn's boss fight was substantially critized by fans, who took issue with his huge hitboxes, high damage, and the speed of his moveset; many deemed Radahn as an unfair boss. As a result Radahn was nerfed in Patch 1.03, with his hitboxes corrected but also lowering his damage. The nerf was partially reversed in Patch 1.03.03, with the damage restored but his hitboxes remaining corrected. His military rank is "General". According to the game files, his horse's name is Leonard.

sections.heading: Crucible Knight Siluria Notes & Other Trivia
sections.text: Siluria seems to have been named after the Silures, an ancient Celcic tribe that lived in present-day Wales. The Silures lived south of the Ordovices, which in turn may have inspired the name of Siluria's counterpart Ordovis . Her name also may reference the Silurian Period, a prehistoic epoch of life that occurred after the end of the Ordovician, much like the Crucible.

sections.text: Stonedigger Troll Fight Strategy The Best Tips for Stonedigger Troll: Use the Kaiden Sellsword Ashes for an easier fight or Spirit Jellyfish Ashes as a distraction. Head northeast out to the balcony and up the stairs to the northwest.

build:blackflame.name: Black Flame Godslayer

build:blasphemous.name: Blasphemous Blade
build:blasphemous.description: Taker’s Flames heals on every wave. Facetanks most of base game. Falls off vs holy resist in SotE.

build:bloodfiends-arm.name: Bloodfiend's Arm
build:bloodfiends-arm.description: The Bloodfiend’s Arm builds Hemorrhage on a big arcane-scaled strike, so each opening both procs bleed and heals you back.

build:bolt-gransax.name: Bolt of Gransax sniper
build:bolt-gransax.description: Ancient Lightning Spear is a long-range nuke with a charged window, so Godfrey Icon and Shard of Alexander both apply. Pair it with a Lightning Nagakiba for the melee.

build:dark-moon.name: Dark Moon Greatsword
build:dark-moon.description: The Moonlight Greatsword beam on the charged heavy is ranged frost damage; Godfrey Icon, Magic Scorpion and Shard of Alexander all stack it. Frostbite then a heavy trade.

build:deaths-poker.name: Death's Poker frost
build:deaths-poker.description: Ghostflame Ignition leaves a patch that keeps ticking, and the charged R2 beam is a safe ranged punish on anything that respects frost.

build:eleonora.name: Eleonora's Poleblade
build:eleonora.description: Bloodblade Dance chains fast Hemorrhage on a dex-arcane twinblade, and the two Winged Insignia talismans ramp the damage as the combo lands.

build:frost-bleed.name: Frost-bleed twinblade
build:frost-bleed.description: A sword with blades on both sides of the hilt. This weapon is difficult to wield, and requires high dexterity. Can be wielded with a single hand, but its true strength is enabled  with dual-handed spinning attacks.
build:frost-bleed.location: Head east from the Agheel Lake South or The First Step Site of Grace to the Dragon-Burnt Ruins in Limgrave.

build:giant-crusher-jump.name: Giant-Crusher jump attack
build:giant-crusher-jump.description: A jump attack from a colossal greathammer does huge stance damage, and Claw plus Axe Talisman both reward the same jumping R2.

build:great-stars-crag.name: Great Stars Cragblade
build:great-stars-crag.description: Cragblade adds stamina damage against guards and poise damage in the open, which a heavy Great Stars turns into constant staggers.

build:greatshield-poke.name: Fingerprint poke
build:greatshield-poke.description: Block with the highest-stability greatshield in the game and poke with a thrusting sword. Safe, boring, and one of the strongest PvE setups there is. Antspur adds Scarlet Rot through the shield.

build:greatsword-lions-claw.name: Greatsword Lion’s Claw
build:greatsword-lions-claw.description: Lion’s Claw is unparryable, has hyper armour, and does real stance damage — on a colossal sword it breaks most bosses in two casts. Pure Strength, no casting stat tax.

build:heavy-bonk.name: Heavy Knight bonk
build:heavy-bonk.description: The pack’s Heavy Knight already has the poise. Giant-Crusher or Anvil Hammer, lion’s claw / cragblade.

build:helphens.name: Helphen's Steeple
build:helphens.description: Helphen’s Steeple buffs itself with ghostflame on the skill, so a strength-int spread gets frostbite pressure and a real melee threat on one weapon.

build:leontiel.name: Leontiel matador
build:leontiel.description: Pack invader weapon. Reach + stance. Pairs with Heavy Knight or a dex hybrid after Radahn.

build:marais.name: Marais Executioner's Sword
build:marais.description: Eochaid’s Dancing Blade spins the sword into a buzzsaw that scales off Arcane, so the arcane-bleed talisman stack lifts the whole skill.

build:meteoric-ore.name: Meteoric Ore arcane
build:meteoric-ore.description: The Ancient Meteoric Ore Greatsword scales off Arcane as well as Strength, so one spread feeds both the weapon and a bleed-heavy talisman set.

build:mimic-status.name: Mimic Tear bleed
build:mimic-status.description: The Mimic copies your bleed kit and doubles the Hemorrhage pressure, so the fight ends before either of you runs out of flasks.

build:moonveil.name: Moonveil Shinobi
build:moonveil.description: Transient Moonlight is a fast ranged slash that staggers at range. Powerstance with a Cold Uchigatana to stack Hemorrhage and Frostbite off the same L1 chain.

build:night-comet.name: Night Comet Sellia
related: Rennala, Queen of the Full Moon
build:night-comet.description: Enemies barely dodge it. Staff of Loss in offhand. Best “I hate lock-on” sorcery.

build:pest-threads-plus.name: Pest-Thread Spears faith
build:pest-threads-plus.description: Pest-Thread Spears hits many times through a big body, and the Dragon Communion Seal turns Arcane into incantation scaling on the same spread.

build:ripple-arc.name: Ripple arcane
build:ripple-arc.description: The Ripple Crescent Halberd scales purely on Arcane, so the whole stat line goes into bleed buildup and Lord of Blood’s Exultation uptime.

build:rivers.name: Rivers of Blood
build:rivers.description: Still deletes most of the Lands Between. Weak to high bleed resist (Malenia is the joke).

build:starscourge.name: Starscourge pull
build:starscourge.description: Starcaller Cry pulls a whole pack into one swing, so the Starscourge Greatsword clears groups and stance-breaks single targets at the same time.

build:sword-night-flame.name: Sword of Night and Flame
build:sword-night-flame.description: Night and Flame stance still gives a ranged magic beam and a close flame sweep, so one weapon covers both ranges without a second catalyst.

build:wing-of-astel.name: Wing of Astel
build:wing-of-astel.description: Nebula is a free ranged burst on a light curved sword, and the weapon still keeps normal dex scaling for the melee you actually land.

sections.text: Adan, Thief of Fire Boss Video Guide [video coming soon] Adan, Thief of Fire Fight Strategy The Best Tips for Adan, Thief of Fire: Magic Glintblade can be used to bait out his rolls, but otherwise any spell can work against him. Equip the Flamedrake Talisman found in the Groveside Cave to reduce Fire Damage taken. Melee Users The biggest challenge for melee players is keeping out of range of Adan's fire spells. Always watch out for the telegraphs. Each fire spell he uses flashes a red circular rune briefly before they are cast, signaling when you should dodge away.

sections.text: The Azula beastmen are anthropomorphic, bestial creatures who reside in Crumbling Farum Azula. They fight using heavy, curved weapons forged from dull iron, and some use shields made from earthenware jars, which are created to make shields. The crumbling ruins of Farum Azula are said to be the remains of a giant mausoleum enshrining an Ancient Dragon, and certain Beastmen, who wield weapons clad in lightning, are chosen to guard it.

Jumping attacks can be a good counter to their charge attack. Melee Users Crucible Knight's attacks are slow and easy to predict, but hit very hard when they land.

sections.text: Demi-Human Chief Fight Strategy The Best Tips for Demi-Human Chief: Try to fight one Demi-Human Chief at a time. sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Malenia, Blade of Miquella**, later known as **Malenia, Goddess of Rot**, is an optional remembrance Boss in Elden Ring. She is a Demigod Shardbearer who is encountered in Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree.

sections.heading: Combat Overview
sections.text: - HP: **33,251** (total) - Defense: **123** - Stance: **80** - She must be parried three times to trigger a stance break, enabling a Critical Hit. - Multiplayer is enabled - Spirit Ashes are enabled - She regains lost HP with every successful attack, even if they are blocked. - She gains +10 Fire negation (0 → 10) and -10 Lightning negation (20 → 10) while standing in water.

sections.heading: Drops
sections.text: - 480,000 runes - Malenia's Great Rune - Remembrance of the Rot Goddess

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - Defeating this boss for the first time unlocks the Shardbearer Malenia achievement. - The "Demigod Slain" flyout is displayed upon defeating Malenia, Goddess of Rot. - Malenia has a prosthetic right arm, left leg, and right foot. These were added due to the infection of the scarlet rot. The rot has also visibly spread over her eyes, so she is presumably also blind. However, her disabilities do not handicap her battle prowess in the slightest. - According to the Scarlet Aeonia Incantation description, Malenia will become a true Goddess if her scarlet flower blooms three times.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Messmer the Impaler** (串刺し公、メスメル, *Kushizashi Kō, Mesumeru*), later known as **Base Serpent Messmer** (邪な蛇、メスメル, *Yokoshimana Hebi, Mesumeru*), is a mandatory remembrance boss in Shadow of the Erdtree.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Messmer is a Demigod who is encountered in the Shadow Keep. He is the source of Messmerfire and the Messmer's Flame incantations. Messmer is **not** an optional boss as he must be defeated in order to acquire Messmer's Kindling that would allow the burning of the Sealing Tree at the Church of the Bud.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - Messmer was likely born earlier than the other Demigods. Exactly when he was born remains unknown, as all mention of him was erased by his mother after she abandoned him in the Land of Shadow. - He is older than Radahn, who was born before Miquella, Malenia, Trina, and Ranni. - Although not explicitly stated, Messmer is strongly implied to be an Empyrean child of Marika and Radagon, born of a single god. - Messmer has the red hair of Radagon and his children. - Messmer was cursed at birth by a threat to Marika's power.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Patches** is an NPC and boss in Elden Ring. He surrenders if you reduce his HP to 50% or less. From then on, he acts as a merchant and gives helpful advice to players.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Patches is a Tarnished who leads a group of bandits, operating out of Murkwater Cave in Limgrave. He is a nomadic and free-spirited individual with a proclivity for tricking people and robbing them of their possessions. If the Tarnished opens the treasure chest in Murkwater Cave, Patches accosts them with accusations of theft. After a brief fight, Patches surrenders and offers his services as a merchant. He reveals that the bandits he leads are former foot soldiers from a defeated army. Later, Patches moves to Liurnia of the Lakes, setting up camp on the Scenic Isle.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - Patches is a reoccurring character in From Software's games, having appeared in *Armored Core: For Answer*, *Demon's Souls*, *Dark Souls*, *Bloodborne*, and *Dark Souls III*. Many of his recognisable traits, such as his physical appearance, use of a spear, and proclivity for tricking the player have been retained for his appearance in *Elden Ring*. - Patches can be summoned during the boss fight against Starscourge Radahn, however he will return to his world after a few seconds.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Grave Warden Duelists**, **Frenzied Duelists**, and **Putrid Grave Warden Duelists** are recurring enemies and bosses in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Duelists are muscular warriors lightly accoutered in bronze armor adorned with serpent effigies, which represent a traitor to the Erdtree. Whether armed with a Duelist Greataxe and iron ball or twin Battle Hammers, they are unrelenting fighters blessed with boundless stamina. During the time of Lord Godfrey, these champions honored the Erdtree by participating in gladiatorial combat at colosseums. Their excited spectators were delighted to see the serpents on their armor get battered and broken. However, the gladiators were banished when the colosseums closed during the age of Lord Radagon.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Dung Eater** is an character in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: A self-described "scourge upon the living," the loathesome Dung Eater is a Tarnished who revels in murder and defilement. He places the Seedbed Curse on his victims to sever their souls from the Erdtree and its grace, trapping them in eternal torment. The Dung Eater has the heart of an Omen without the body to match. He wears a malformed set of hefty red armor with tufts of red hair emerging from the bleeding stumps of its severed Omen horns. His helmet has no opening except for a deep gash over the right eye.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - Roderika cautions the spiritual harm done by the Dung Eater's Seedbed Curse is worse than Godrick's grafting. - The Dung Eater possesses a fate. - During the intro cinematic, the Dung Eater is hung by an iron chain in a gallows, silhouetted against the bright Erdtree or sun. A faint golden Grace near his chest illuminates the sun medallion, visually linking it to the haloed backdrop. - He was confined to the same prison as nobleborn Omen beneath the streets of Leyndell. Like the Omen, his body also contains cursed spirits.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Revenger** was an unseen character in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: The nameless revenger was a champion who lived during the Age of the Erdtree, when Godfrey reigned as Elden Lord. After the golden armies of the Erdtree decimated his clan, he vowed vengeance and returned to Castle Morne. There, he collected the swords of his fallen kin and forged them into a single massive blade—the Grafted Blade Greatsword. He challenged Lord Godfrey during the Siege of Castle Morne, but was slain by Queen Marika's Grace-given champion.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - The revenger likely belonged to the Stormveil faction that once controlled Limgrave and the Weeping Peninsula. They may be the rebellion-starting laborer-turned-champion whose Brick Hammer is found at Stormveil Castle. They were said to have had the strength of a giant. - Serosh, Lord of Beasts appears on the Grafted Blade Greatsword's hilt. - Castellan Edgar, a Banished Knight in Godrick's service, refuses to abandon Castle Morne until the Grafted Blade Greatsword is reclaimed from the Leonine Misbegotten.

sections.text: Maleigh Marais is the Lord of the Shaded Castle, a location that has been overseen by executioners for generations. He was once a private worshipper of scarlet rot, and would later become obsessed with Malenia. This is partly due to his own sickly bloodline, fueling an admiration of Malenia for remaining strong despite her own affliction. The state of the Shaded Castle reflects this shift in fixation, as the Castellan's Hall is filled with prostheses, Cleanrot armor, and a large portrait of Malenia.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Millicent** is an NPC cooperator in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Millicent is a red-haired woman afflicted by Scarlet Rot. She and her sisters were found in the Swamp of Aeonia in Caelid by Sage Gowry, who raised them as his daughters. Her four sisters travelled to Miquella's Haligtree under Gowry's guidance, however Millicent alone remained behind. At Gowry's behest, the Tarnished obtains an Unalloyed Gold Needle and brings it to the Church of the Plague, where Millicent is slowly succumbing to the Rot. She inserts the needle to stall the Rot, regaining her strength.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - Millicent's questline can still be started even after defeating Malenia. - The Valkyrie's Prosthesis links Millicent and Malenia through the symbolic loss of the right arm. Statues of Malenia at Haligtree Town depict her in her youth without a right arm. None of Millicent's Sisters meet this criteria.

invader:millicents-sisters.name: Millicent's Sisters

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Millicent's sisters** are adopted daughters of Sage Gowry and siblings of Millicent. These red haired girls once sprouted as buds from the Scarlet Aeonia found within the heart of Caelid. They all wear the Traveler's Set and use weapons and skills associated with either aspects of their inadvertent mother Malenia, both her role as the unalloyed blade of Miquella and her looming transformation into the goddess of rot. They all seek to aid their adoptive father in cultivating Millicent into a Scarlet Valkyrie. __TOC__

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: All sisters can be found in Elphael, Brace of the Haligtree towards the end of Millicent's questline. To reach them the player needs to: - 1. Retrieve the snapped Unalloyed Gold Needle by defeating Commander O'Neil in the Heart of Aeonia. - Optional: Polyanna, Adopted Daughter can be summoned as a cooperator to assist in this fight. - 2. Give the snapped needle to Sage Gowry at Gowry's Shack so that he may repair it. - 3. Reload the area by either: - A. Resting at/teleporting to a Site of Grace - B. Exit to the Main Menu and then enter back into the game. - 4.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - Maureen's Treespear is unique and impossible to replicate by the player as it has Charge Forth. Instead the version the player has access to cannot be infused with Ashes of War and it has Sacred Order as it's default skill.

sections.heading: Effect
sections.text: - Activate to invade the world of another player as a Bloody Finger, with three consumable Phantom Bloody Fingers to use in that session. - If the invading player has activated Mohg's Great Rune, they will also receive three Phantom Great Runes to use in that session.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Preceptor Miriam** is a hostile character in Elden Ring. Miriam can be fought twice in the Carian Study Hall, once before placing the Carian Inverted Statue and once after.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Preceptor Miriam, as indicated by the name, is a teacher of sorcery at the Carian Study Hall. She served the Carian royals in the past and now guards the hall from intruders.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - She rather predictably wears the Preceptor Set, using the standard chest and head pieces. - Wields an Academy Glintstone Staff which she uses to cast Carian Slicer, Greatblade Phalanx, Loretta's Greatbow, and Magic Downpour, of which the Greatbow spell is usually the most used. - Can teleport to the next spot in her area upon taking sufficient damage, though she may skip over a spot in the Standard Study Hall if enough damage is taken at one spot. This cannot happen in the Inverted Study Hall unless killed in the first spot, as she only has two spots there.

sections.heading: Drops
sections.text: - Lucidity (only in the inverted version of the Carian Study Hall) - Magic Downpour (only in the normal version of the Carian Study Hall)

sections.heading: Elden Ring Sanguine Noble Boss Guide
sections.text: Sanguine Noble Fight Strategy The Best Tips for Sanguine Noble: Bring Stanching Boluses Item Melee Users For melee users, be wary as the Sanguine Noble's swings are very fast, so it's recommended that you use a fast one-hand weapon like a straight sword or an axe. Every single type of attack this boss does stacks bleed so it's best that you bring Stanching Boluses . Do not rush this boss and be careful with its string of stabs and slashes. sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Vargram the Raging Wolf** is an NPC in *Elden Ring*.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Vargram was one of the first Tarnished to visit Roundtable Hold. He earned his nickname from the white wolf pelt that adorns his helm. Vargram aspired to attain the status of a wolf, based on the old legend that wolves are shadows of the Empyreans. Vargram was a friend of Errant Sorcerer Wilhelm, however guidance led the two into confrontation with one another, and Wilhelm was taken prisoner in Roundtable Hold. The Tarnished encounters Vargram and Wilhelm together in the Fortified Manor in Leyndell, Royal Capital, during a joint mission with Knight Bernahl on behalf of the Volcano Manor.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **White Mask Varré** (白面のヴァレー) is an NPC in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Varré is an enigmatic man who dresses as a war surgeon. War Surgeons, despite their name, are not surgeons or doctors. They act as mercy killers on battlefields, putting dying soldiers out of their misery as quickly as possible by delivering final blows. Varré was a war surgeon prior to his association with Mohg. Varré was abducted by Mohg against his will along with various other war surgeons, however it was noted that Varré was particularly talented with blood incantations, and that of all the war surgeons abducted he was the only one able to "tame" Mohg's cursed blood.

sections.heading: Location
sections.text: - Limgrave (The First Step) Just past the Site of Grace. Will leave a message in his spot after talking with Finger Reader Enia at the Roundtable Hold. - Liurnia of the Lakes (Fallen Ruins of the Lake) At the entrance of the Rose Church, to the west of the Site of Grace. - Mohgwyn Palace (Dynasty Mausoleum Entrance) His invasion sign is located in the hallway before the Dynasty Mausoleum Midpoint Site of Grace. After defeating him, Varré will be found laying on the floor close to where the sign previously was.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: The **Brick Hammer** is a Melee Armament in Elden Ring.

sections.heading: Acquisition
sections.text: **Location**: Stormveil Castle - The Brick Hammer is found on a corpse in Stormveil Castle in the area within the wall past the Stormveil Cliffside site of grace. It is accessed by climbing the ladder behind the door unlocked by the Rusty Key and turning right to jump across the gap, crossing the beams, and then jumping to another platform leading to an opening in the wall. Follow the path outside and reenter at the round tower. The corpse hangs from a ledge.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - The Brick Hammer is a Great Hammer. - This weapon may reference the Revenger.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.text: **Patches** is an NPC and boss in Elden Ring. He surrenders if you reduce his HP to 50% or less. From then on, he acts as a merchant and gives helpful advice to players.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.text: Patches is a Tarnished who leads a group of bandits, operating out of Murkwater Cave in Limgrave. He is a nomadic and free-spirited individual with a proclivity for tricking people and robbing them of their possessions. If the Tarnished opens the treasure chest in Murkwater Cave, Patches accosts them with accusations of theft. After a brief fight, Patches surrenders and offers his services as a merchant. He reveals that the bandits he leads are former foot soldiers from a defeated army. Later, Patches moves to Liurnia of the Lakes, setting up camp on the Scenic Isle.

sections.heading: Notes
sections.text: - Patches is a reoccurring character in From Software's games, having appeared in *Armored Core: For Answer*, *Demon's Souls*, *Dark Souls*, *Bloodborne*, and *Dark Souls III*. Many of his recognisable traits, such as his physical appearance, use of a spear, and proclivity for tricking the player have been retained for his appearance in *Elden Ring*. - Patches can be summoned during the boss fight against Starscourge Radahn, however he will return to his world after a few seconds.

mechanic:affinities.name: Weapon affinities
mechanic:affinities.description: An affinity changes a weapon’s damage type and scaling: Heavy favours Strength, Keen favours Dexterity, Quality uses both, and Magic and Cold add Intelligence. Fire and Flame Art add fire with Strength and Faith scaling respectively, Lightning is Dexterity, and Sacred is Faith. Blood, Poison and Occult scale with Arcane.

mechanic:ashes-of-war.name: Ashes of War
mechanic:ashes-of-war.description: This Ash of War grants an armament the Sacred affinity and the following skill:"Golden Vow: Skill passed down from antiquity among the knights of the capital. Raise armament aloft and pledge to honor the Erdtree in battle, granting self and nearby allies increased attack power and defense."Usable on all melee armaments.
mechanic:ashes-of-war.location: An Ash of War grants a weapon a skill and, on most armaments, lets you choose its affinity. Applying one overwrites the previous skill and affinity, and some Ashes can be duplicated for a second copy with Lost Ashes of War. Unique weapons and many boss weapons cannot take Ashes at all.

mechanic:attack-rating.name: Attack rating (AR)
mechanic:attack-rating.description: Attack rating, or AR, is the total damage number a weapon shows across every damage type it deals, after the character’s stats are applied through scaling. Buffs, enemy negation and status buildup are not part of the displayed AR. The number the game shows is the summed damage types floored, matching the AR calculator the app uses.

mechanic:buff-stacking.name: Buff stacking
mechanic:buff-stacking.description: Buffs fall into categories such as aura, body, weapon and shield, and two buffs from the same category overwrite each other. Golden Vow is an aura and Flame, Grant Me Strength is a body buff, so they stack with each other and with a weapon grease. The Wondrous Physick supplies another independent layer.

mechanic:co-op.name: Co-op & Furlcalling Finger Remedy
mechanic:co-op.description: Item for online play. Craftable item. Reveals cooperative and competitive multiplayer signs. Co-op summoning signs will be shown in gold, while hostile summoning signs will be shown in red. Multiplayer begins when you summon a player from another world through their sign.

stats.Effect: Reveals co-op and hostile summoning signs

mechanic:co-op.location: A Furlcalling Finger Remedy reveals summon signs left by other players, which you touch to call a cooperator. A password lets you link with a specific friend regardless of level, and the host’s session is what the group plays in. Co-op disables Torrent and Spirit Ashes and opens the world to invaders.

mechanic:crafting.name: Crafting & cookbooks
mechanic:crafting.description: Leather bag containing a pestle and mortar, small blade, and various other tools. Enables item crafting from the main menu. Provides both means to fight and means to survive.

stats.Effect: Enables the practice of item Crafting

mechanic:crafting.location: The crafting kit lets you turn gathered materials into throwables, pots, greases, arrows and perfumes. Cookbooks unlock new recipes, and each one is found in a specific place or sold by a merchant. Crafted pots and perfumes are among the best status and burst tools in the game.

mechanic:critical-hits.name: Backstabs, ripostes & critical hits
mechanic:critical-hits.description: A critical hit multiplies your weapon’s attack rating rather than adding a flat amount. Backstabs land from directly behind an unaware or outmanoeuvred enemy, while ripostes follow a successful parry or a stance break. The Misericorde is the classic critical weapon because of its very high critical modifier.

mechanic:damage-types.name: Damage types
mechanic:damage-types.description: Physical damage splits into standard, strike, slash and pierce, and enemies resist each differently. Elemental damage comes as magic, fire, lightning and holy, and a weapon can carry a physical component plus one or more elements. The type matters more than the number against a boss with a lopsided negation.

mechanic:defense-negation.name: Defense & negation
mechanic:defense-negation.description: Defense is the flat number that shaves damage off every hit, while negation is the percentage that reduces what is left. Physical defense comes mostly from your stats and armour, and elemental negation comes from armour and talismans. Because the two apply in sequence, stacking a matching negation talisman can blunt a boss’s signature element.

mechanic:equip-load.name: Equip load classes
mechanic:equip-load.description: Your equipped weight as a share of maximum equip load decides your roll. Under thirty percent you light roll with the most distance, from thirty to seventy you medium roll, and above seventy you heavy roll with a long recovery. Going over one hundred percent overloads you and slows movement to a crawl.

mechanic:flask-charges.name: Flask charges (Golden Seeds)
mechanic:flask-charges.description: A golden seed, found at the base of an illusory tree.

stats.Effect: Increases Sacred Flask's number of uses

mechanic:flask-charges.location: Golden Seeds increase the number of charges in your Flask of Crimson Tears and Flask of Cerulean Tears. The first seed or two cost one each and later upgrades cost more, so a full run needs thirty seeds. The two flask types share the same total charge pool.

mechanic:flask-potency.name: Flask potency (Sacred Tears)
mechanic:flask-potency.description: Blessing of the Erdtree, worshiped in the churches of all lands; this

stats.Effect: Improves Sacred Flask's potency

mechanic:flask-potency.location: Sacred Tears upgrade the potency of both flasks, healing more per Crimson charge and restoring more FP per Cerulean charge. There are twelve Sacred Tears and each adds one upgrade level. Full potency makes a flask heal roughly twice a starting flask.

mechanic:great-runes.name: Great Runes
mechanic:great-runes.location:
**Location**: Lands Between
- **About Great Runes** is automatically acquired upon defeating a Shardbearer and obtaining a Devoid Great Rune for the first time.

mechanic:guard-boost.name: Blocking & guard boost
mechanic:guard-boost.description: Blocking an attack absorbs part of its damage and drains stamina based on your shield’s guard boost. A higher guard boost means less stamina lost per blocked hit, which lets you hold the line and set up guard counters. Greatshields and the Greatshield Talisman push guard boost highest.

mechanic:guard-counter.name: Guard counter
mechanic:guard-counter.location:
**Location**: Cave of Knowledge
- **About Guard Counters** is automatically acquired upon approaching the Soldier of Godrick boss in the Cave of Knowledge.

mechanic:hyperarmor.name: Hyperarmor
mechanic:hyperarmor.description: Hyperarmor is temporary immunity to being staggered during specific attack animations. It is granted by the move itself, not by your poise, so a colossal swing can power through a hit that would interrupt a lighter weapon. Your poise still decides whether damage that lands outside those frames staggers you.

mechanic:incantation.name: Incantations
mechanic:incantation.location:
**Location**: Cave of Knowledge
- **About Sorceries and Incantations** is automatically acquired after concept introduction.

mechanic:invasions.name: Invasions
mechanic:invasions.description: Item for online play. Lures in invaders. This allows your world to be invaded without any Furled Finger cooperators present, and it also shortens the interval between windows of opportunity for invasion. Additionally, enables the arrival of a second invader. (When two invaders are present, you will be limited to one cooperator.)

stats.Effect: Lures in invanders.

mechanic:invasions.location: Bloody Fingers and Recusant Fingers let you invade a host’s world to fight for runes and rewards. The Taunter’s Tongue invites invaders into your own world, and the Blue Cipher Ring calls hunters to defend a host in trouble. Invaders are always outnumbered and downscaled when the host has cooperators.

mechanic:jump-attacks.name: Jump attacks
mechanic:jump-attacks.description: A jumping heavy attack leaps in, hits hard, does solid stance damage and has a short recovery. It is the safest way to punish a boss because you are already moving out of range as the swing ends. The Claw Talisman boosts jump attack damage and the Raptor’s Black Feathers add another jump-attack bonus.

mechanic:larval-tears.name: Rebirth & Larval Tears
mechanic:larval-tears.description: After defeating Rennala you can ask her to rebirth your character, redistributing every level you have spent. Each rebirth costs one Larval Tear, which are found through the world and bought from a few merchants. Your level total and collected gear do not change, only where the points sit.

mechanic:map-fragments.name: Map fragments
mechanic:map-fragments.description: Map of the western region of Limgrave. The demesne of Limgrave, far south of the Erdtree, is bordered to the northwest by the cliffs of Stormveil, and under its ever-clouded skies roll the great steppes of the pale lands.

stats.Effect: Map of Limgrave's western region.

mechanic:map-fragments.location: Each region’s map is blank until you collect its Map Fragment from a stele marked on the map edge. Until then you can still travel and explore, but you have no map of the area. Collecting the fragment reveals the terrain, graces and many markers for that region.

mechanic:matchmaking.name: Co-op & PvP matchmaking
mechanic:matchmaking.description: Summon range is decided by both your rune level and the highest-upgraded weapon you have ever held. That weapon memory means a low-level character who picked up a late-game weapon can only be matched with tougher players. A password overrides both limits and downscales the stronger player to the host.

mechanic:memory-slots.name: Memory slots & Memory Stones

stats.Effect: Increases memory slots

mechanic:memory-slots.location: Memory slots decide how many sorceries and incantations you can have equipped at once. Each Memory Stone you find adds one slot, and the starting count depends on your class. The cap is ten slots once every stone is collected.

mechanic:ng-plus.name: NG+ scaling
mechanic:ng-plus.description: Starting Journey 2 keeps your level, gear, items and most graces but makes every enemy tougher and worth more runes. The difficulty climbs each cycle up to Journey 7, after which it stops rising. Some quest items and key items are reset, so re-earn anything a quest needs.

mechanic:parry.name: Parrying
mechanic:parry.location: A parry deflects an incoming attack during a short window and leaves the attacker open to a riposte. Small shields and the Parry Ash of War have the widest timing, while medium shields and weapons parry poorly or not at all. Some attacks, including many grabs and colossal swings, cannot be parried.

mechanic:point-of-no-return.name: Point of no return
mechanic:point-of-no-return.description: Resting at the Forge of the Giants and burning the Erdtree permanently changes the world. Leyndell becomes the Ashen Capital, several quest lines close and some items can no longer be obtained. The app warns before this and other gates so you can finish what matters first.

mechanic:poise.name: Poise
mechanic:poise.description: Poise is the hidden stat that decides whether an incoming hit interrupts your attack or cast. Every hit drains poise by that attack’s poise damage; reaching zero staggers you and briefly opens you up. Poise refills on its own after roughly thirty seconds without being hit.

mechanic:powerstance.name: Powerstancing
mechanic:powerstance.description: Equipping two weapons of the same class, one in each hand, unlocks paired attacks that swing both at once. The L1 chain and the jumping L1 hit with both weapons, stacking status buildup and stance damage in a single swing. It costs more stamina than a normal attack line.

mechanic:revered-spirit-ash.name: Revered Spirit Ash
mechanic:revered-spirit-ash.description: Revered Spirit Ashes raise the Revered Spirit Ash Blessing, which strengthens your summoned spirits in the Realm of Shadow. It is a separate track from the Scadutree Blessing and only affects summons, not you. It runs to level ten with twenty-five ashes.

mechanic:rune-arc.name: Rune Arc
mechanic:rune-arc.description: A shard of the shattered Elden Ring.

stats.Effect: Grants the blessing of an equipped rune upon use

mechanic:rune-arc.location: A Rune Arc activates the Great Rune you have equipped at a Site of Grace. The effect lasts until you die, so a careful player can keep one running for a long stretch. Rune Arcs drop from co-op and invasion wins as well as from enemies.

mechanic:rune-loss.name: Rune loss & recovery
mechanic:rune-loss.description: When you die you drop all carried runes at the spot where you fell. Return and touch them to recover the lot; die again before that and the first drop is gone for good. A Sacrificial Twig in your inventory prevents the loss once.

mechanic:scadutree-blessing.name: Scadutree Blessing
mechanic:scadutree-blessing.location:
**Location**: Realm of Shadow
- The About the Scadutree Blessing is added to the inventory upon collecting a Scadutree Fragment for the first time.

mechanic:scaling-letters.name: Scaling letters
mechanic:scaling-letters.description: The letter beside a stat on a weapon shows how strongly its AR grows from that stat, running E, D, C, B, A, S from weakest to strongest. The grade is a band of the weapon’s stored scaling coefficient, so S adds far more per point than E. Upgrading a weapon usually raises these coefficients, which is why a weapon can climb a letter as it is reinforced.

mechanic:sites-of-grace.name: Sites of Grace
mechanic:sites-of-grace.location:
**Location**: Site of Grace
- **About Fast Travel to Sites of Grace** is automatically acquired upon resting at a Site of Grace for the first time.

mechanic:soft-cap-endurance.name: Endurance soft caps
mechanic:soft-cap-endurance.description: Endurance raises stamina as well as maximum equip load. Stamina gains are largely done past thirty and effectively stop at fifty, but the equip-load curve keeps climbing all the way to ninety-nine. That is why a heavy build may keep investing long after a light one stops.

mechanic:soft-cap-mind.name: Mind soft caps
mechanic:soft-cap-mind.description: Mind raises your FP pool and therefore how many spells, Ashes of War and summons you can chain before drinking. The FP gains slow down after forty and nearly stop after sixty. Casters usually stop at forty early and push toward sixty later.

mechanic:soft-cap-offensive.name: Offensive stat soft caps
mechanic:soft-cap-offensive.description: Strength, Dexterity, Intelligence, Faith and Arcane all scale weapon and spell damage through breakpoints around twenty, sixty and eighty. Points before twenty are the most efficient, the stretch to sixty is the main investment, and gains past eighty are small. Matching the weapon’s own scaling letters is what makes a point pay off.

mechanic:soft-cap-vigor.name: Vigor soft caps
mechanic:soft-cap-vigor.description: Vigor is the stat that buys you mistakes, and it is the first one most builds should push. Its HP gains fall off sharply after forty, then again after sixty, so points spent past the second cap return very little. Sixty Vigor is a common endgame target for a comfortable health pool.

mechanic:sorcery.name: Sorceries
mechanic:sorcery.description: Sorceries are cast with a staff and scale with Intelligence, with a few exceptions that dip into other stats. They cost FP and are gated by the staff’s stats and upgrade level as well as your own. Glintstone magic is the core family, with frost and gravity branches.

mechanic:spirit-ashes.name: Spirit Ashes
mechanic:spirit-ashes.location:
**Location**: Caelid Colosseum
- The **About Combat with Spirit Ashes** is automatically acquired upon interacting with Marika's Effigy inside the Caelid Colosseum for the first time.

mechanic:stamina.name: Stamina
mechanic:stamina.description: Stamina is spent on attacks, rolls, running, jumping and blocking. It regenerates after a short delay and the rate is raised by the Green Turtle Talisman and similar effects. Running out mid-swing usually means eating the next hit, so manage the bar rather than mashing.

mechanic:stance-break.name: Stance break
mechanic:stance-break.location:
**Location**: Cave of Knowledge
- **About Stance-Breaking** is automatically acquired toward the end of the Cave of Knowledge.

mechanic:stat-requirements.name: Stat requirements
mechanic:stat-requirements.description: Each armament and catalyst lists minimum Strength, Dexterity, Intelligence, Faith and Arcane. Failing a requirement cuts your damage sharply and can make the weapon bounce off enemies, even though you can still swing it. Two-handing lowers the Strength requirement you need to meet.

mechanic:status-bleed.name: Blood loss (bleed)
mechanic:status-bleed.description: Blood loss drains a percentage of the target’s maximum HP plus a flat amount when the bar fills. It scales with Arcane on most blood-affinity weapons and is the fastest way to delete a high-health boss. Because resistance rises after each proc, bleed builds pair best with rapid multi-hit attacks.

mechanic:status-buildup.name: Status buildup & resistance
mechanic:status-buildup.description: Status effects fill a hidden bar as hits land, and the effect triggers when the bar fills. After it triggers the bar empties and your resistance to that status rises, so the same effect takes longer the next time. Buildup also decays gradually while you are not being hit.

mechanic:status-death-blight.name: Death blight
mechanic:status-death-blight.description: Death blight kills the target outright when the bar fills, with no saving throw. It is rare from the player side and mostly appears on certain enemies and in PvP. Its bar decays quickly, so it must be applied in a burst.

mechanic:status-frostbite.name: Frostbite
mechanic:status-frostbite.description: Frostbite deals burst damage and temporarily lowers the target’s absorption, so follow-up hits land harder. It can trigger again after a cooldown, and cold affinity weapons also keep a physical component. Fire damage removes the frost debuff early, so avoid mixing the two.

mechanic:status-madness.name: Madness
mechanic:status-madness.description: Madness damages both HP and FP and staggers the victim when it triggers. It only affects humanoid, Tarnished-descended enemies, so it does nothing to most beasts and monsters. In PvP it is one of the strongest burst windows in the game.

mechanic:status-poison.name: Poison

stats.Effect: Cures Poison ailment and reduces poison build-up.

mechanic:status-poison.location: Poison applies a damage-over-time effect that ticks down the target’s HP for a set duration. The stronger variant is Deadly Poison, which does more damage per tick. Poison scales with Arcane and is best used to soften a boss you expect to fight for a while.
mechanic:status-poison.description: Incantation of the Two Fingers' faithful.

mechanic:status-scarlet-rot.name: Scarlet rot
mechanic:status-scarlet-rot.description: Scarlet rot is a stronger damage-over-time than poison and is the signature tool of Caelid and the Haligtree. A rot proc ticks for a large share of health over a short window, which makes it ideal against bosses with huge health pools. Boluses and Preserving Boluses cure it.

mechanic:status-sleep.name: Sleep
mechanic:status-sleep.description: Craftable item prepared using a cracked pot. Filled with the incantations of St. Trina. Consumes FP. Throw at enemy to release a purple, soporific haze. Like a lullaby, or a quagmire, it irresistibly draws its victims down into sleep. Sweet dreams.

stats.Effect: Emits a Soporific purple haze

mechanic:status-sleep.location: Sleep incapacitates the target for a short time, letting you land free hits or reposition. It only works on enemies that are not immune, and any damage wakes them, so it is a control tool rather than a damage tool. Sleep Pots are the usual delivery method.

mechanic:stealth.name: Stealth
mechanic:stealth.description: Crouching lowers the noise you make and the distance at which enemies notice you, and tall grass hides you completely. From behind, an unaware enemy can be backstabbed or simply walked past. The Crepus’s Vial and similar talismans improve stealth further.

mechanic:summoning-pools.name: Summoning pools
mechanic:summoning-pools.location:
**Location**: Summoning Pools
- **About Summoning Pools** is automatically acquired upon obtaining either the Small Golden Effigy or Small Red Effigy for the first time.

mechanic:talisman-slots.name: Talisman slots
mechanic:talisman-slots.description: Small, withered bag, knitted by hand. Bestowed upon the ruling lord, or those atempting to become lord, by the elderly Finger Reader.

stats.Effect: Increases Talisman equip slots.

mechanic:talisman-slots.location: You begin with a single talisman slot and expand it with Talisman Pouches found through the run. Four slots is the maximum, which is why a build’s talismans are a real trade-off rather than a checklist. Talismans apply their effect continuously with no FP cost.

mechanic:torrent.name: Torrent
mechanic:torrent.location: Torrent is the spectral steed summoned with the Spectral Steed Whistle. He can double jump and is much faster than running, which makes open-world travel and many field bosses easier. Torrent is banned inside most legacy dungeons and boss arenas and cannot be used in co-op.

stats.Effect: Creates crystal mass that fires stream of crystal shards

mechanic:two-handing.name: Two-handing
mechanic:two-handing.description: Holding a weapon in both hands multiplies your effective Strength by one and a half, rounded down. That raises both the Strength scaling of the weapon and your effective Strength for meeting its requirement, letting a lower-Strength build wield heavy armaments. It does not change Dexterity, Intelligence, Faith or Arcane.

mechanic:upgrades.name: Upgrades & smithing
mechanic:upgrades.description: Regular armaments upgrade to plus twenty-five with Smithing Stones and somber armaments to plus ten with Somber Smithing Stones. The final step of either track needs an Ancient Dragon Smithing Stone from a late-game or optional boss. Spirit Ashes upgrade the same way with Grave Glovewort and Great Grave Glovewort.

mechanic:weapon-scaling.name: Weapon scaling
mechanic:weapon-scaling.description: Every weapon scales its attack rating with one or more stats, shown as a letter grade from E up to S. Levelling the stats the weapon actually uses, and upgrading the weapon, raises that contribution. A weapon with high base damage and poor scaling wants minimum stats, while an S-scaling weapon rewards heavy investment.

mechanic:whetblades.name: Whetblades
mechanic:whetblades.description: Glintstone whetblade with a cipher engraved. Can be used as a whetstone knife.

stats.Effect: Grants choice of affinity upgrade to weapon

mechanic:whetblades.location: A Whetblade unlocks extra affinity choices when you apply an Ash of War, regardless of the Ash you use. The Iron Whetblade gives Heavy, Keen and Quality; Glintstone gives Magic and Cold; Red-Hot gives Fire and Flame Art; Sanctified gives Sacred; and the Black Whetblade gives Blood, Poison and Occult.

mechanic:wondrous-physick.name: Wondrous Physick
mechanic:wondrous-physick.description: A relic of the physick chemists, priests of the Erdtree. Harnesses the powers of crystal tears, which only form after the passage of many moons. Various specials effects are bestowed upon the drinker, dependent on the specific mixture of crystal tears. Rest at a site of grace to replenish. It is said that in the Lands Between, pools of crystal tears amass at the bases of Minor Erdtrees.

stats.Effect: Bestows various special effects

mechanic:wondrous-physick.location: The Flask of Wondrous Physick holds two Crystal Tears that you choose and mix at a Site of Grace. Drinking it applies both effects at once and the flask refills whenever you rest, so it is a free burst buff each attempt. Tears range from flat stat boosts to the famous Cerulean Hidden Tear that removes FP costs.

sections.heading: Elden Ring Commander Gaius Location
sections.text: Commander Gaius can be found at the back of the Shadow Keep legacy dungeon. To reach him, you must enter from the east through the Church District . Map Link<br>

sections.heading: Commander Gaius Combat information
sections.text: Health: 33,871 HP Defense: 123 Stance : 100 Parryable : No Is vulnerable to a critical hit after being stance broken Damage: Standard , Slash , Strike , Pierce , Magic Drops 230,000, Remembrance of the Wild Boar Rider Negations (or Absorptions) Standard 20 Slash 40 Strike 20 Pierce 20 Magic 20 Fire 0 Lightning 0 Holy -20 The negation numbers are the % of your damage that gets blocked. For example, if a negation is 60, 40% of that damage by that type will go through and 60% will be negated. Bigger number = less damage.

sections.heading: Elden Ring Commander Gaius Boss Guide
sections.text: Commander Gaius Boss Video Guide Commander Gaius Fight Strategy The Best Tips for Commander Gaius: Use the Black Knife Tiche Ash Summons Opt for a Great Hammer like the Heavy Curved Great Club Bring Flask of Wondrous Physick ( Greenburst Crystal Tear and Opaline Hardtear or Windy Crystal Tear ) Item Use Crucible Feather Talisman to make dodging his charge easier Melee Users Before you begin the fight, make sure to replenish your Flask by resting at the nearest Site of Grace.

region:limgrave.location:

region:shadow.name: Realm of Shadow
region:shadow.location:
**Trade:** Remembrance of the Shadow Sunflower
- Exchange the Remembrance with Finger Reader Enia at Roundtable Hold.
  - The remembrance is acquired by defeating the Scadutree Avatar.
  - After the Remembrance is acquired, a Wandering Mausoleum or Remembrance Duplication Coffins can be used to duplicate it. The spell can only be acquired once per new game cycle, regardless of how many remembrances are held.

region:weeping.name: Weeping Peninsula
region:weeping.location:

- Map: Weeping Peninsula is located in front of a Guide Stele south of the  Castle Morne Rampart Site of Grace, along the main road leading towards Castle Morne.
